# Steps to Create a Non-Public | Public IP VM

REMINDER: How to Create/Reset Azure & Tenable Credentials

[Requesting Access (and Resetting Credentials) to Tenable and Azure](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ebi7mDIADegs7fFd2FAR-Pwp9c5SO056C-4HygFmLmw/edit?tab=t.0)

## Azure Virtual Machine Overview

Sign into Azure: [https://portal.azure.com](https://portal.azure.com)

  

Resource Groups (optional/educational)

- Observe your “Resource Group”, used for storing your VMs and other resources you will create in the vulnerability management course and SOC analyst course
    

- It’s basically a folder to organize your stuff
    

- Some admin access over VMs and a few other things
    
- Observe your permissions
    
- Observe Cyber Range VMs
    

  

Virtual Machines

Create only ONE (1) virtual machine. If you create more than one VM at a time, the cyber range automation will wipe out your resource group. This is to prevent people from creating a ton of VMs and bankrupting me, lol

- If you want to be nice to me, please delete your VMs when you’re done using them
    
- All VMs will automatically be shutdown at 3am PST
    

Please delete your VMs when you are finished :)

  

How to Create Virtual Machines:

Basics Tab:

  

- Check which Cyber Range you belong to — Cyber Range 1, 2, 3, or 4.
    

Look for your student Resource Group (student-rg-xxxxx).

Example: student-rg-121fd3fdf663c83d6f31553bb2aa7597dd8301b068e51dbdb1031dc…

  

Where you see your student-rg listed, that is your assigned Cyber Range.

Select that Cyber Range and choose your own Resource Group only.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)  
  

- Availability Options: No infrastructured redundancy required
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)  
  

- Region: MUST be East US 2  
    ![](data:image/png;base64,)  
      
    
- Image: Windows 11 Pro or Ubuntu Server
    

Note: Since support for Windows 10 has ended, it no longer receives security updates or maintenance from Microsoft. We recommend using Windows 11 Pro.

  

- If you chose Ubuntu Server, for Authentication type, choose [X] Password  
    ![](data:image/png;base64,)  
      
      
    

- Disk Size: Size should be Standard_D2als_v6 (or whatever is available)  
    (You may have to click See all sizes)  
    ![](data:image/png;base64,)  
      
    
- Licensing: MUST agree
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

Disks Tab:

- OS disk type: MUST be Standard SSD 
    

  

Note: For a Linux VM (Ubuntu) the default OS disk size is typically 30 GB, For Windows and other images you will often see a default OS disk around 127 GB.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

Networking Tab:

- The Cyber Range subscription you belong to (1, 2, 3, or 4) must match the network where you will add your VM.
    

  

For example:

If you belong to Cyber Range 2, your VNet should look like:  
Cyber-Range-2-VNet  
  

Your Subnet should also match, such as:  
Cyber-Range-2-Subnet

  
If the correct VNet is not showing, verify the Region and Resource Group under the “Basics” tab.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

   

-  It is no longer required to create a Public IP address with your VM as you can now connect to the VMs with Azure Bastion ([instructions here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OZf0pB3GqhTriou5VHvv5liPUC3vnfFwZI60xvVfWIE/edit?tab=t.0), but we will cover this later). For “Public IP” select “None” unless you are intentionally wanting the VM to be exposed to the internet for some reason. If you don’t know what I’m talking about, just select “None”. The reason for this, Public IPs are limited. If you know you need one for some reason, you can create one, but otherwise, select none.
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

- NIC network security group: Basic OR Advanced -> “NSG-Wide-Open”, depending on what you want to do
    
- [ ] Delete public IP and NIC when VM is deleted 
    

  

Monitoring Tab:

- Boot diagnostics: [X] Disable
    

  

Review + Create

- If your VM creation fails for some reason, go to your resource group and clean it up before trying again. I might add automation to do this for you in the future.
    
- You are able to reset your password
    
- Observe Resource Group items after VM successfully created
    

  

Post Creation

- Observe Password Reset (Virtual Machines → Help → Reset Password)
    
- Observe Resources in Resource Group
    

- If you create more VMs than allowed, the contents of your Resource Group will be wiped
    

  

How to Turn Off Virtual Machine

- Go to your Resource Group, click the Virtual Machine
    
- Click turn off or [Stop]
    

  

How to Delete / Virtual Machine Cleanup

- Go to your Resource Group, click the Virtual Machine, and Delete
    
- Possible to leave components behind, so just check for them in your Resource Group and delete them
    

  

How to Connect to Your Virtual Machine

[How to Connect to a Virtual Machine Using Azure Bastion](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OZf0pB3GqhTriou5VHvv5liPUC3vnfFwZI60xvVfWIE/edit?tab=t.0)
